title: Unions
instructions: A union looks like a struct, but with a twist: all its members SHARE the same space. It can hold ONE of them at a time.
You'd use a union to save memory when a value could be one of several types, but never more than one at once.
Writing to one member overwrites the others, because they're literally the same spot in memory.
Here, we store an int, then store a float in the same union — the float replaces the int.
task: Store 3.5 in the union's as_float member so the output ends with:  as float = 3.5
hint:
Assign to the float member with a dot:

    v.as_float = 3.5;
